ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has coordinate axes and two broken-line graphs composed of mutually perpendicular rays. The graph labeled y=f(x) is an upward-opening V shape, with its vertex at (-1,0) on the x-axis, and its right branch passes through (0,1) near the y-axis. The graph labeled y=g(x) is a downward-opening V shape, with its vertex at (1,0) on the x-axis, and its left branch passes through (0,-1) near the y-axis. Reasoning: Consider g(x+2), which means translating the graph of g left by 2 units, so the vertex of g moves from (1,0) to (-1,0), consistent with the horizontal position of the vertex of f. After translation the graph still opens downward, while f opens upward, so multiplying by -1 again is equivalent to reflection about the x-axis. In this way the graph of -g(x+2) completely coincides with the graph of f. Because both functions are defined on all real numbers, and the two rays extend to cover all x, for every real number x there is f(x)=-g(x+2).

method.method_draft: Use graph transformations. From the image, read that the graph of f is an upward V with vertex at (-1, 0), while the graph of g is a downward V with vertex at (1, 0). The text says both functions are defined for all real x and each graph is made of two perpendicular halflines, so comparing the whole V-shapes is valid. Shift the graph of g left by 2 units by considering g(x+2); its vertex moves from (1, 0) to (-1, 0), matching f's vertex horizontally. Since g is downward-opening and f is upward-opening, reflect g(x+2) across the x-axis by multiplying by -1. The resulting graph matches f for every x, giving f(x) = -g(x+2).

method.method_draft: Write formulas from the plotted V-shapes. From the image, f has vertex (-1, 0), rises with slope 1 to the right, and rises with slope -1 to the left, so f(x) = |x+1|. The graph of g has vertex (1, 0), rises with slope 1 on the left side and falls with slope -1 on the right side, so g(x) = -|x-1|. Substitute x+2 into g: g(x+2) = -|(x+2)-1| = -|x+1|. Therefore -g(x+2) = |x+1| = f(x), so the equality satisfied for every real x is f(x) = -g(x+2).
